items.title: Incident Cardiovascular Disease and Associated Risk Factors in Iranian Adults: Findings from a Prospective Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are among the main causes of premature mortality. This study aimed to identify independent determinants of CVD incidence and to examine the associations of different risk factor domains, including renal, cardiometabolic, and lifestyle factors, with incident CVD using sequential Cox regression models. This population-based prospective cohort study was conducted on 9411 individuals without a history of cardiovascular disease from the Kharameh cohort. Participants were followed for a total of 888,867 person-months, and new CVD cases were identified based on medical records and standard ICD-10 codes. Sequential Cox proportional hazards regression models were fitted by adding blocks of covariates. During a mean follow-up of 7.87 years (SD, 1.32), 530 new CVD cases were recorded (incidence rate: 5.96 per 10,000 person-months). In the final adjusted model, older age, male sex, employment status, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, higher waist-to-height ratio, elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL), and current smoking were associated with incident CVD. The sequential addition of renal, cardiometabolic, and lifestyle factors improved model fit, with the AIC decreasing from 9285.3 in the initial model to 9114.1 in the final model. In this population-based cohort study, demographic, cardiometabolic, and lifestyle factors were associated with incident CVD. Diabetes, hypertension, and current smoking showed particularly strong associations with CVD incidence. The sequential addition of renal, cardiometabolic, and lifestyle factors improved model fit, highlighting the contribution of multiple risk factor domains to the assessment of CVD risk in this population.

items.title: Microbiota-associated post-translational remodeling of immune cell states in gastrointestinal cancer.
items.abstract: Microbial communities influence gastrointestinal (GI) cancer through metabolic exchange and immune regulation. Post-translational modifications (PTMs) can connect these signals to changes in chromatin, protein function and immune-cell states. This narrative review examines histone and non-histone modifications to explore how microbial inputs and host metabolism intersect in the regulation of immune-cell states and tumor immunity. Microbial metabolites can influence acyl-donor availability and PTM enzyme activity, while microbial sensing can reprogram host metabolism and downstream modification states. These routes provide a framework for understanding changes in lymphoid and myeloid cell function, whose consequences for tumor immunity depend on cellular and disease context. Among the studies assessed, evidence linking microbial interventions to immune-cell PTM changes in GI cancer is concentrated in colorectal cancer and its metastatic models. Findings from nonmalignant models, other cancers and host metabolic studies provide complementary insights into potentially relevant mechanisms. Their extension to microbiota-immune interactions in GI tumors requires attention to both microbial involvement and the functional contribution of specific modifications. Understanding how microbial inputs converge with host metabolism at the level of PTM regulation may reveal opportunities to modulate tumor immunity. Defining metabolite sources and cellular exposure, resolving the functions of individual modifications, and validating pathways in relevant anatomical and therapeutic settings will be important for identifying mechanisms that can inform biomarker and therapeutic development.

items.title: Marked QT Prolongation and Torsades de Pointes Following Pulsed Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
items.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is increasingly used for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), but its effects on ventricular repolarization remain incompletely understood. A man in his 70s with persistent atrial fibrillation, a left ventricular ejection fraction of 18%, previous nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, and three months of amiodarone therapy underwent PVI using the FARAPULSE system (Boston Scientific Corporation, Marlborough, MA, USA). Approximately one month before PFA, automated electrocardiographic measurements showed a QT interval of 316 ms and a corrected QT interval (QTc) of 395 ms. One hour after PFA, the QT/QTc values were 356/431 ms. On postoperative day one, the QT/QTc values increased to 602/610 ms, accompanied by frequent premature ventricular contractions and a serum potassium concentration of 3.2 mEq/L. On postoperative day two, telemetry demonstrated a short-long-short sequence immediately before torsades de pointes, which was initiated by a premature ventricular contraction when the QT/QTc values were 490/510 ms and serum potassium was 3.0 mEq/L. Altered consciousness developed, and one 150-J direct-current shock terminated the arrhythmia. After potassium and magnesium replacement, no recurrence occurred. The QTc decreased to 479 ms on postoperative day four and 403 ms at one month. The event was probably multifactorial; severe ventricular dysfunction, residual amiodarone effects, hypokalemia, and transient postprocedural hypoxemia prevent attribution of causality to PFA alone. Nevertheless, the marked but reversible QT prolongation after the procedure supports careful monitoring of the QT interval, ventricular ectopy, and electrolytes after PFA in susceptible patients.

items.title: High temperature polymer dielectrics: materials, mechanisms and capacitive energy storage.
items.abstract: Electrostatic capacitors are widely used in hybrid electric vehicles, aerospace electronics, and high power pulsed systems because of their high power density, rapid charge discharge capability, and excellent cycling stability. Continued advances in transportation electrification and the miniaturization of power electronics demand capacitors that retain reliable energy storage performance at increasingly high temperatures and electric fields, placing stringent requirements on polymer dielectrics. At elevated temperatures, accelerated charge carrier generation and transport markedly increase leakage conduction and dielectric loss, leading to rapid deterioration in breakdown strength ( E b ), energy storage performance, and long term operational stability. Developing polymer dielectrics that simultaneously offer high thermal stability, high discharged energy density ( U d ), high discharging efficiency ( η ), and long term reliability is therefore imperative. Polymers with high glass transition temperatures ( T g ) exhibit promising thermal stability and electrical insulation, but their polarization, conduction loss, breakdown behavior, and processability under coupled thermal and electrical stresses require further optimization. This review surveys comprehensive recent advances in high temperature polymer based dielectrics for capacitive energy storage. It first establishes the relationships among the dielectric constant ( ε r ), E b , dielectric loss, long term operational stability, self-healing capability, U d , and η . Representative strategies based on high T g polymers, crosslinked polymer networks, all organic composite dielectrics, and newly designed molecular backbones are then critically assessed, alongside emerging artificial intelligence (AI) assisted approaches to polymer discovery and multi-objective optimization. Finally, outstanding challenges in suppressing high temperature conduction loss, elucidating breakdown self-healing mechanisms, ensuring long term reliability, standardizing high temperature evaluation, and manufacturing large area, high quality films are identified and future priorities for translating advanced polymer dielectrics from laboratory studies into practical capacitors are discussed.

items.title: Association of aggregate index of systemic inflammation with mortality in coronary artery disease patients without sepsis and application of a nomogram model.
items.abstract: To investigate the association between the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI) and short- and long-term all-cause mortality in coronary artery disease (CAD) patients without sepsis, and to develop and internally validate an AISI-based nomogram for predicting 30-day mortality. This retrospective study included 2,386 CAD patients without sepsis. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations between AISI and 30-, 90-, 180-, and 365-day mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves compared survival across AISI quartiles. Restricted cubic spline analyses assessed linearity, and receiver operating characteristic curves evaluated discrimination. A nomogram incorporating AISI and clinical variables was developed using LASSO and multivariate logistic regression and validated with discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Higher AISI was associated with increased mortality risk. Survival differed significantly across AISI quartiles (Log-rank p 0.05), with moderate discrimination. The nomogram including AISI, age, lymphocyte count, creatinine, SOFA, cerebrovascular disease, and respiratory failure showed strong performance (AUC 0.870 training; 0.848 testing) and clinical utility. AISI independently predicted all-cause mortality in non-septic CAD patients, and an AISI-based nomogram may improve risk stratification.

items.title: Dynamic immunoengineering: mechanobiology and stimuli-responsive biointerfaces in regeneration and cancer: a comprehensive review.
items.abstract: Mechanobiology and stimulus-responsive bio-interfaces have emerged as transformative technologies that allow sophisticated and precise regulation of immune cells for tissue regeneration and cancer therapies, thus driving a paradigm shift in immunoengineering. This review highlights how cell responses to mechanical stimuli contribute to regulating the immune system through integrin signalling, mechanosensitive ion channels, and the YAP/TAZ signalling axis. An overview of smart biomaterials' designing strategies for sensing mechanical stiffness, temperature, pH, redox status, light, electricity, and enzymatic action is provided, and the roles of smart biomaterials in regeneration of bone, cartilage, skin, nervous tissue, and tumour micro-environment modulation are discussed. Preclinical and clinical evidence suggest that the compounds can drive macrophage polarisation, increase T cell activation, and contribute to the overcome of specific tumour immune escape mechanisms in preclinical ​studies. This also takes on the challenge of bio-material-centered cancer immunotherapy. This involves looking at various types of implantable device, from a new nano-based anti-cancer platform to construct arrays to get greater delivery specificity and minimise side effects, to different combinatorial strategies against cancer. Although there have been promising results, the difficulty issues such as the spatial-temporal heterogeneity of the pathological micro-environment and the processing complexity and regulation problems still challenge the widespread application and implementation. Integration of AI with sophisticated in vitro models suggested for acceleration of translation. The future perspective envisages a closed-loop bio-interface made up of biosensors for dynamic and on-line immunomodulation. These interdisciplinary confluences provide tremendous potential for the field to shift the role of biomaterials from a passive scaffold to an active, programmable immune regulator, thereby developing next-generation personalized regenerative medicine and oncology therapeutics.

items.title: The dual role of Fusobacterium nucleatum in colorectal cancer: from oncogenic mechanisms to immunotherapy sensitization.
items.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum ( Fn ) has emerged as a critical microbial modulator in the development, progression, and therapeutic response of colorectal cancer (CRC). High-resolution genomic evidence identifies Fn subsp. animalis Clade 2 ( Fna C2) as the predominant clade enriched in tumor microenvironments and invasive biofilms, favored by Fna C2-specific metabolic adaptations (utilizing ethanolamine and 1,2-propanediol) and a glutamate-dependent acid resistance (GDAR) system. At the molecular level, Fn drives oncogenesis, inflammation, and metastasis via the FadA/β-catenin and Fap2/TIGIT pathways, as well as the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/MyD88/NF-κB/microRNA-21 (miR-21) axis that suppresses RAS GTPase-activating protein 1 (RASA1) to hyperactivate RAS signaling. Fap2-mediated invasion further triggers interleukin-8 (IL-8) and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 1 (CXCL1) secretion, recruiting myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and neutrophils to foster a pro-tumor niche. Additionally, Fn confers chemoresistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) through BIRC3 (an inhibitor of apoptosis protein) upregulation and autophagy pathways. Paradoxically, Fn also acts as a "double-edged sword" by sensitizing microsatellite stable (MSS) CRC to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This immunosensitization is mediated via a dual pathway: cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-STING activation enhancing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), and microbial butyrate acting as a histone deacetylase 3/8 (HDAC3/8) inhibitor to epigenetically reprogram CD8+ T cells against exhaustion. To address the spatial heterogeneity and the safety risks of live bacterial therapy, translational efforts are pivoting toward cell-free interventions such as postbiotics and STING agonists. This review comprehensively delineates the clade-specific traits of Fna C2 alongside broader Fn immunomodulatory mechanisms, highlighting its potential and current limitations as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in precision CRC care.

items.title: Enhanced Immunogenicity of Newcastle Disease Virus Using Antigen Antibody Immune Complex in Chicken.
items.abstract: Antigen-antibody immune complex (Ag-Ab) was analyzed for its ability to mediate a humoral immune response in broiler chicks against Newcastle disease virus. The immune complex was developed using an optimum ratio of an antigen and antibody. The comparative immune response of experimental immune complexes and market-available vaccines was demonstrated in semi-SPF chicks. All hundred (one-day-old) chicks were reared and divided into five groups including live vaccine, immune complex, inactivated vaccine, immune complex with a booster dose, and unvaccinated control group. Geometric mean antibody titers were obtained through a hemagglutination inhibition test at the weekly interval. All the groups were challenged with the virulent Newcastle disease virus 28 th day postvaccination. The study demonstrated that the geometric mean antibody titers of the immune complex booster dose group (1:630) were significantly higher than all the other groups on the 28 th day (live group [1:315], immune complex [1:512], inactivated [1:256]). It was concluded that the immune complex response was significantly higher ( p < 0.05) and persistent with complete protection as compared to the already available live and inactivated vaccine groups. Therefore, the immune complex antigen may be a promising candidate for providing better protection and immunogenicity in birds.

items.title: Social determinants of health and breast cancer disparities in the United States: a multilevel review of barriers to diagnosis and treatment.
items.abstract: US breast cancer mortality has more than halved since 1975, but the decline has not been shared equally. Black women's death rates remain 36% higher than White women's, and rates among American Indian and Alaska Native women have not fallen in three decades. Within-subtype survival gaps are widest in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative disease, where sustained treatment matters most, a pattern more consistent with unequal access than with biology alone. We conducted a narrative review with a structured, documented search of US evidence (PubMed, 2010 to 2026, prespecified eligibility criteria) on five domains of social determinants of health: insurance status and healthcare access, neighborhood socioeconomic deprivation, structural racism, geographic access, and individual socioeconomic status. We present them as four interrelated levels (upstream structural determinants, neighborhood and geographic exposures, health-system and access mediators, and individual socioeconomic consequences) and examine two outcomes, stage at diagnosis and guideline-concordant treatment, labeling estimates by design and outcome definition. In registry and national database analyses, uninsured women had 2.6-fold higher odds of stage IIIB to IV disease than privately insured women, and late-stage diagnosis fell after Medicaid expansion in quasi-experimental comparisons. Neighborhood deprivation was associated with later stage and, in mediation analyses, statistically accounted for about 45% of the Black-White difference in all-cause mortality; historical redlining was associated with higher mortality, roughly half mediated by present-day neighborhood conditions. Rural residence carried a small excess of later stage and a larger deficit in radiation receipt linked to travel distance. Compared with private insurance, Medicaid or no insurance was associated with less breast conservation and reconstruction, more omission of radiation, lower receipt of guideline-concordant chemotherapy, earlier discontinuation of endocrine therapy, and lower uptake of immunotherapy. Most evidence is observational, and area-level measures assigned to individuals risk contextual misclassification. Patient navigation improves screening uptake and diagnostic timeliness in trials but has no demonstrated survival benefit; Medicaid expansion is associated with earlier stage, timelier treatment and lower mortality in difference-in-differences analyses. Simulation modeling suggests equalizing treatment access would narrow, not close, the mortality gap. Closing it requires attention to coverage design, neighborhood investment, and oncology workforce distribution.

items.title: Exosome-mediated macrophage polarization in pulmonary diseases: heterogeneity, signaling crosstalk, and translational challenges.
items.abstract: Although exosomes and macrophages have been studied in lung diseases, an integrated framework linking exosomal cargo, macrophage heterogeneity, disease stage, and translational barriers is still lacking. Pulmonary diseases cause substantial morbidity and mortality, and the pulmonary immune microenvironment is shaped by complex cell-cell communication. Lung macrophages are key innate immune cells that display a spectrum of activation states, including M1-like, M2-like, and intermediate phenotypes. This review provides an integrated framework linking exosomal cargo, lung macrophage heterogeneity, signaling crosstalk, disease stage, and translational barriers. We summarize exosome biogenesis and lung macrophage ontogeny, focusing on how exosomes regulate macrophage polarization through NF-κB, PI3K/AKT, JAK/STAT, and ERK pathways and their crosstalk. We then discuss context-dependent effects in lung injury, COPD, asthma, pulmonary fibrosis, and lung cancer. We also review exosome engineering strategies for targeted macrophage modulation. Despite advances, clinical translation is limited by large-scale purification, targeted delivery, safety, and standardized quality control. We conclude that exosome-mediated macrophage regulation is context-dependent and promising, but translation requires MISEV-compliant exosome terminology, rigorous evidence grading, scalable manufacturing, and safe targeted delivery.

items.title: Diagnosis and treatment outcomes of childhood TB in Zanzibar.
items.abstract: Childhood TB often goes undiagnosed due to non-specific clinical and radiological signs and suboptimal performance of available diagnostics. We aimed to assess the diagnostic practices and treatment outcomes of childhood TB in Zanzibar. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using secondary individual-level surveillance data from the Electronic TB and Leprosy Register. Children aged below 15 years with TB who were notified from January 2019 to December 2024 were included in this study. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise demographic characteristics, diagnostic methods, and treatment outcomes. From January 2019 to December 2024, a total of 838 children with TB were included. Median age was 4 years, 474 (56.6%) were male, and 34 (4.1%) were children living with HIV. Bacteriological confirmation was achieved in 56 (6.7%) children, with children with confirmed TB being predominantly older than children without confirmed TB. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra was the common bacteriological confirmation test (91.1%), with overall GeneXpert use increasing over time, alongside declining reliance on clinical score charts. Treatment outcomes were excellent, with 98.1% treatment success. Although treatment outcomes are highly successful, bacteriological confirmation is still uncommon. Expanding access to molecular diagnostics and other recommended tools could improve childhood TB diagnosis and control in Zanzibar.

items.title: Improved Acceptance of Vitamin K in Neonates After an Intervention, in a Community Healthcare System.
items.abstract: Parents refuse intramuscular administration of vitamin K for their newborns for various reasons. This study seeks to characterize the incidence of intramuscular vitamin K refusal in a community hospital, and the acceptance of vitamin K after a parental education. Additionally, to study the incidence of refusal of hepatitis B vaccination and erythromycin ocular prophylaxis in newborns. Demographic data, parental beliefs were prospectively collected, and specific factors associated with refusal of intramuscular vitamin K were compared between parents who refused and a control group of parents who accepted vitamin K. An educational intervention was applied to parents who refused vitamin K prophylaxis. The association of refusal among vitamin K administration, hepatitis B vaccination and erythromycin ocular prophylaxis was examined. 767 newborns were included and 30 (3.9%) did not receive intramuscular vitamin K. Neonatal female sex (O.R. = 2.4, 95% C.I.: 1.0-5.5) and maternal white, non-Hispanic race (O.R. = 4.7, 95% C.I: 1.2-20.9) were associated with vitamin K refusal. Conversely, primipara status (O.R.: = 0.3, 95% C.I.: 0.1-0.9) and maternal anxiety and/or depression (O.R. = 0.4, 95% C.I: 0.1-1.0) were associated with more acceptance. After an educational intervention, 7 of 22 (32%) of families who initially denied, accepted the intramuscular administration of vitamin K. Among families who refused vitamin K, all refused neonatal hepatitis B vaccination; 27 (90%) refused erythromycin prophylaxis as well. A significant rate of refusal of intramuscular vitamin K administration in neonates was observed and was associated with female sex and maternal white, non-Hispanic race and reversely with primipara and maternal emotional status. Close monitoring and development of interventions are needed, as many of these parents are amenable to education and change. Parents refuse intramuscular administration of vitamin K for their newborns for various reasons, and this is correlated with various factors including vaccine refusal. No specific intervention to address vitamin K refusal has been studied. What is added: In North Dakota, a high rate of refusal of intramuscular vitamin K administration in neonates was observed and was associated with female sex and white race and reversely with primipara status and maternal emotional status. It is also highly associated with refusal of hepatitis B vaccination and erythromycin ocular prophylaxis. “Not necessary” and concerns about pain and side effects are main reasons for denial. Almost one third of parents may be convinced after a simplified intervention that is described.

items.title: Sequential Plasma Exchange and Tacrolimus for Probable Autoimmune Hepatitis Presenting As Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure.
items.abstract: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an immune-mediated inflammatory liver disease that may first become apparent through severe decompensation of previously unrecognized cirrhosis. We report a 46-year-old woman with probable AIH (simplified diagnostic score 6), culture-negative spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, marked jaundice, and subsequent West Haven grade III hepatic encephalopathy despite corticosteroid therapy. Liver and cerebral failure were consistent with European Association for the Study of the Liver-Chronic Liver Failure grade 2 acute-on-chronic liver failure, conditional on the clinical diagnosis of cirrhosis. Liver transplantation was unavailable locally. Five therapeutic plasma exchange sessions produced an initial improvement in bilirubin and neurological status, but asterixis and hyperbilirubinemia recurred after an approximately nine-day interval. Three further exchanges were followed by tacrolimus at 1 mg twice daily. At the last follow-up, encephalopathy had not recurred, and aminotransferases had improved, although marked cholestasis and mild ascites persisted. Plasma exchange may provide temporary support while further treatment is established, but this observation cannot isolate its effect from concurrent immunosuppression and infection management.

items.title: Association of VCTE-derived liver parameters and MASLD subtypes with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome.
items.abstract: In cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is not included in its staging criteria. We aimed to evaluate the associations between vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE)-derived liver parameters and advanced CKM stages, and to examine whether the CKM profile differs among MASLD subtypes. VCTE and cardio-metabolic assessments were conducted among individuals enrolled in the New Hong Kong Cardiovascular Risk Factor Prevalence Study (NCRISPS), an ongoing population-based cohort recruiting Chinese residents of Hong Kong SAR between 2019 and 2024. Among 3199 eligible participants, 37.2% had MASLD, with 34.4% having MASLD alone and 2.8% due to combined etiology. VCTE-derived controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness (LS), and FibroScan-AST (FAST) score each showed graded associations with advanced CKM stages (all P<0.05). Compared to participants without steatotic liver disease, those with MASLD alone (adjusted OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.94; P = 0.016) and MASLD due to combined etiology (adjusted OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.22-4.49; P = 0.010) were both associated with significantly higher odds of advanced CKM stages. MASLD, with and without combined etiology, was associated with the presence of advanced CKM syndrome. VCTE-derived parameters including CAP, LS, and FAST score were all associated with advanced CKM stages in a graded manner and whether inclusion of these non-invasive markers improves CKM syndrome staging and classification warrants longitudinal evaluation.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of glucocorticoid therapy for hepatitis B virus-related liver failure.
items.abstract: To assess the clinical efficacy and safety of short-term glucocorticoid therapy in patients with early- or pre-stage hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related liver failure. We retrospectively analyzed 143 patients with early- or pre-stage HBV-related liver failure treated at our center between January 2015 and December 2025. Of these, 43 received methylprednisolone conventional therapy (glucocorticoid group) and 100 received conventional therapy alone (conventional group). We analyzed the trends in total bilirubin (TBil), prothrombin time activity (PTA), and albumin (ALB) between the two groups during the initial 4 weeks, as well as 4-week clinical improvement, 12-week mortality, complications, and HBV-DNA changes. The glucocorticoid group showed faster TBil decline and earlier PTA improvement (both P   P  = 0.002) and lower 12-week mortality (2.3% vs. 27/0%, P  = 0.005). Glucocorticoid therapy was independently associated with 4-week improvement (OR = 4.21) and with a significantly lower risk of death (OR = 0.074). Overall complications were fewer in the glucocorticoid group (37.2% vs. 62.0%, P  = 0.006). No significant between-group differences were observed in HBV-DNA levels at baseline or week 4 ( P  = 0.389 and P  = 0.584, respectively). For patients with early or pre-stage HBV-related liver failure, adding short-term methylprednisolone to traditional therapy accelerates the recovery of liver function, improves short-term outcomes, and reduces mortality without a statistically significant increase in complications;no significant increase in HBV-DNA was observed during the 4-week observation period.

items.title: Active surveillance strategy for low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN): 5-year results.
items.abstract: Low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (LAMNs) are rare tumors with potential progression to pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP). The optimal management of patients without macroscopic peritoneal disease remains debated. We previously reported 3-year outcomes of an active surveillance (AS) strategy. This study evaluates the 5-year results of the same cohort. This prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary referral center. Patients with histologically confirmed LAMN, normal postoperative MRI and tumor markers, and limited or no extra-appendiceal mucin were enrolled in an AS protocol. Surveillance included clinical examination, serum tumor markers, and abdominopelvic MRI at 6 months and annually thereafter. Disease progression was defined as histologically proven PMP. Among the 30 patients initially included, 25 completed a mean 5-year follow-up and 5 were excluded after exceeding 75 years of age. No new PMP cases occurred among patients disease-free at 3 years. All four patients previously suspected of radiologic progression underwent cytoreduction and HIPEC; only two (8 %) had histologically confirmed low-grade PMP and achieved remission after complete cytoreduction. Two cases were false-positive imaging findings. After 5 years, active surveillance remains a safe and effective long-term strategy for selected patients with LAMN, supporting conservative MRI-based follow-up and avoiding unnecessary aggressive surgery.

items.title: Muscle and tissue radiodensity matter: Automated CT-based body composition analysis predicts survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients undergoing degradable starch microspheres transarterial chemoembolization (DSM-TACE).
items.abstract: Transarterial chemoembolization with degradable starch microspheres (DSM-TACE) has emerged as an increasingly important and effective treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, the impact of body composition on clinical outcomes remains unknown. This study aimed to assess the prognostic significance of pretreatment, fully automated 3D-volumetric computed tomography (CT)-based body composition analysis (BCA) in patients with HCC undergoing DSM-TACE. Retrospective single-center study. A total of 137 patients were treated with repetitive DSM-TACE. BCA quantified the volumes and radiodensities of the skeletal muscle (SM), visceral adipose tissue (VAT), subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT), and bone (B) using baseline abdominal CT scans. The maximally selected log-rank test was applied for the cutoff selection. Survival outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and uni- and multivariate Cox proportional hazards models with hazard ratios (HR). The median overall survival (OS) of the cohort was 16.5 months. Multivariate analysis identified three BCA parameters as independent predictors of improved survival: a high SM/B ratio (HR: 0.44; p = 0.008), high SM radiodensity (HR: 0.26; p = 0.004), and low VAT radiodensity (HR: 0.20; p = 0.004). A cumulative risk score based on these independent factors (1 point per favorable factor) allowed for distinct survival stratification ( p p ≤ 0.016). Survival stratification remained statistically significant in both the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage B and C subgroups. Fully automated CT-based quantification of body composition is a valuable tool for assessing survival in patients with HCC treated with DSM-TACE. The integration of the SM/B ratio and tissue radiodensities enable can improve personalized survival stratification within the BCLC B and C subgroups, warranting further validation and clinical integration evaluation. Transarterial chemoembolization with degradable starch microspheres (DSM-TACE) is an established treatment for patients with liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC), but survival after therapy varies widely. It is not yet clear whether differences in body composition, such as muscle, fat, or bone tissue, influence outcomes. In this study, 137 patients with HCC treated with repeated DSM-TACE were analyzed. Routine abdominal CT scans performed before treatment were evaluated using a fully automated computer-based method to measure muscle, fat, and bone characteristics. The researchers examined whether these measurements were associated with patient survival. The median survival time was 16.5 months. Four body composition features were linked to longer survival: a higher muscle-to-bone ratio, higher muscle radiodensity, and lower radiodensity of visceral fat. Using these factors, a simple risk score was created that clearly separated patients into groups with very different survival times, ranging from almost four years in the lowest-risk group to only a few months in the highest-risk group. This survival difference was also observed in patients with more advanced disease stages. These findings show that automated analysis of standard CT scans can provide useful information about prognosis in patients with liver cancer undergoing DSM-TACE and may support more personalized treatment decisions in the future.

items.title: Lower triglyceride-glucose index is independently associated with multidrug-resistant organism infection in patients with pyogenic liver abscess: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a surrogate marker of insulin resistance, has been linked to various infectious outcomes. However, no prior research has explored its independent association with multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) infection among patients with pyogenic liver abscess (PLA). This retrospective cohort study aimed to investigate the relationship between TyG index and MDRO infection identified at or during the index admission in hospitalized PLA patients. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 440 PLA patients. The association between the TyG index and MDRO infection was evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression, adjusting for a comprehensive panel of confounders, including severity of illness proxies. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed to determine the predictive value of the TyG index, and restricted cubic splines (RCS) were used to examine the dose-response relationship. Interactions were examined via subgroup analysis, and adjusted odds ratios (ORs) accompanied by 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were depicted in a forest plot. MDRO infection was identified in 40 (9.1%) patients, including one patient that was simultaneously infected with both ESBL-KP and E. coli . After full multivariate adjustment (Model III), continuous TyG index exhibited a significant inverse independent association with MDRO infection: per standard deviation (SD) elevation of TyG index, the adjusted OR (aOR) was 0.470 (95% CI: 0.298-0.742). Relative to the lowest TyG tertile (T1, reference group), patients in the second (T2) and third (T3) tertiles presented markedly reduced MDRO odds, with aORs of 0.244 (95% CI: 0.095-0.628) and 0.241 (95% CI: 0.089-0.655), respectively. RCS modeling showed a declining relationship without statistically significant non-linearity (non-linear p -value = 0.233); because a non-significant non-linearity test does not establish linearity, and MDRO rates were similar in T2 (5.4%) and T3 (6.7%), the pattern is best characterized as threshold-like, with risk concentrated in the lowest TyG range. The TyG index yielded modest predictive accuracy for MDRO infection, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.629. Subgroup interaction analyses detected no significant effect modification across all stratified clinical subgroups (all interaction p -values ranged from 0.146 to 0.864 in adjusted models). Among PLA patients, reduced TyG index independently correlates with elevated risk of MDRO infection. These novel findings reveal an inverse association of uncertain mechanism between host metabolic status and MDRO infection risk in PLA.

items.title: Dose optimisation of carboplatin in the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen for HER2-Positive breast cancer: a real-world dose-response analysis using restricted cubic splines.
items.abstract: The docetaxel-carboplatin-trastuzumab-pertuzumab (TCbHP) regimen is widely used as a standard neoadjuvant strategy for HER2-positive breast cancer and provides substantial pathologic complete response (pCR) benefits. However, evidence on the optimal balance between treatment efficacy and toxicity remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the dose-response relationship between carboplatin exposure and pCR and to explore its association with treatment-related adverse events. In this retrospective study, clinical data were collected from patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who received the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen followed by surgery at two tertiary hospitals between January 2019 and December 2023. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models and Firth's bias-reduced penalized-likelihood logistic regression analyses were applied to assess the association and dose-response relationship between actual carboplatin exposure (dAUC) and pCR after adjustment for relevant confounders. Among 153 eligible patients, 107 (69.9%) achieved pCR. Patients with pCR had significantly higher carboplatin exposure compared with those without pCR. RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear dose-response relationship between carboplatin dAUC and pCR probability (overall trend p = 0.050; non-linearity p = 0.114), with an exploratory exposure threshold of 5.49 mg min/mL. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that higher carboplatin exposure, as measured by dAUC, was independently associated with reduced odds of achieving non-pCR. However, excessively high carboplatin exposure was significantly associated with an elevated risk of thrombocytopenia, while patients who experienced liver injury exhibited lower carboplatin exposure. Carboplatin exposure showed a linear association with pCR in patients receiving the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen. Low exploratory exposure (5.49 mg min/mL) may compromise treatment efficacy, while excessively high exposure may increase hematologic toxicity. These findings provide real-world evidence to support individualized carboplatin dosing strategies aimed at optimizing the efficacy-toxicity balance.

items.title: 10-year follow-up of a patient with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma and concomitant Henoch-Schönlein purpura nephritis, with metachronous liver and brain metastases: a case report.
items.abstract: Brain metastasis from high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) is rare, and serum Carbohydrate Antigen 125 (CA125) monitoring has limited surveillance value in this setting. Clinical evidence guiding the diagnosis and management of patients with such rare clinical presentations and comorbidities remains limited. We report a patient with HGSOC (FIGO stage IIIB) who was followed for 10 years, from the initial diagnosis in 2016 to the latest follow-up in October 2026. She was clinically diagnosed with Henoch-Schönlein purpura nephritis (HSPN), complicated by synchronous HGSOC. She underwent cytoreductive surgery followed by docetaxel plus carboplatin (TC) chemotherapy. In 2018, HSPN recurred concurrently with surgical-site recurrence and hepatic metastasis. Following chemotherapy, HSPN remitted without specific immunosuppressive treatment, while the hepatic lesions achieved near-complete remission. In 2021, she developed a solitary left occipital brain metastasis, and her clinical symptoms improved after surgical resection, whole-brain radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Intracranial tumor recurrence was confirmed in 2022. Genetic testing in 2023 identified a pathogenic germline mutation in breast cancer susceptibility gene 1 ( BRCA1 ), with positive homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status. She subsequently received pamiparib-based therapy, including combination treatment with bevacizumab. At the latest follow-up, she remained neurologically asymptomatic with an ECOG performance status of 1. This case demonstrates a temporal association between HSPN activity and the clinical course of HGSOC, raising the possibility of a tumor-associated immune phenomenon. In addition, prolonged disease control was observed during treatment with pamiparib plus bevacizumab in this patient with HGSOC brain metastasis harboring a pathogenic germline BRCA1 mutation and HRD positivity.
